# archestra_oauth_client_federated_credential (Resource)

Workload identity federation trust for an `archestra_oauth_client` with `grant_type = "client_credentials"`: an OIDC token whose issuer, audience, subject and listed claims all match exactly can be sent as the `client_assertion` of a client credentials grant at `/api/auth/oauth2/token` instead of the client secret. Changing the issuer, audience, subject or claim conditions revokes the access tokens the credential already issued, as does destroying it. Requires an Enterprise license.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Let a GitHub Actions workflow on `main` sign in as an OAuth client with the
# job's own OIDC token, sent as the client assertion of a client credentials
# grant, so the repository stores no client secret.
#
# Every value matches exactly; there are no wildcards. To trust a second
# branch, workflow or environment, declare a second credential (a client
# holds up to 20). Only a client with grant_type "client_credentials" can
# have federated credentials.
resource "archestra_oauth_client" "deployer" {
  name                     = "Deployment automation"
  scopes                   = ["llm:proxy"]
  grant_type               = "client_credentials"
  include_future_providers = true
}

resource "archestra_oauth_client_federated_credential" "example" {
  oauth_client_id = archestra_oauth_client.deployer.id
  name            = "acme/infra deploy workflow on main"
  issuer          = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  # The job requests its token with this audience, usually the Archestra URL.
  audience = "https://archestra.example.com"
  subject  = "repo:acme/infra:ref:refs/heads/main"

  # Optional: other claims the token must carry. Pin the workflow file and
  # the repository's immutable ID, so a renamed or recreated repository of
  # the same name is not trusted.
  claim_conditions = {
    job_workflow_ref = "acme/infra/.github/workflows/deploy.yml@refs/heads/main"
    repository_id    = "123456789"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `audience` (String) Value the token's `aud` claim must carry, usually the Archestra URL.
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer URL, exactly as the token's `iss` claim carries it (for GitHub Actions, `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`). Must be reachable over https at a public address.
- `name` (String) Credential display name, unique within the OAuth client.
- `oauth_client_id` (String) `archestra_oauth_client` the token signs in as.
- `subject` (String) Value the token's `sub` claim must equal (for GitHub Actions, for example `repo:acme/infra:ref:refs/heads/main`). No wildcards.

### Optional

- `claim_conditions` (Map of String) Other claims the token must carry, each with the exact value required (for example `job_workflow_ref` or `repository_id`). Defaults to none.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Composite OAuth client ID and credential UUID.
- `last_used_at` (String) Most recent successful sign-in with the credential.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import archestra_oauth_client_federated_credential.example oauth_client_id:credential_uuid
```
